expectations.text: Uses cub unit import with --where-resource (not kubectl get -o yaml piped into cub unit update)
expectations.evidence: Uses kubectl get all -o yaml piped into a file then cub unit update. Does not know about cub unit import.

expectations.text: Pre-creates Units and binds to Target before importing
expectations.evidence: Creates Unit but does not bind to Target before import. Worker/Target setup comes after.

expectations.text: Splits resources into multiple Units per import-unit-granularity (namespace, policy, workloads)
expectations.evidence: One Unit for everything. No splitting by ownership or lifecycle.

expectations.text: Uses import.include_cluster = true for the Namespace (cluster-scoped)
expectations.evidence: No mention of import.include_cluster or cluster-scoped resource handling.

expectations.text: Reviews imported data for cluster-added defaults and admission-webhook artifacts
expectations.evidence: No review step for defaults or cleanup.

expectations.text: Establishes config-as-data discipline (no more kubectl apply, use cub-mutate + cub-apply)
expectations.evidence: Mentions cub unit apply but no config-as-data doctrine. Still proposes 'cub unit update < updated-payments.yaml' as the change flow.
No Worker health check. Worker setup happens after import.

expectations.text: Uses valid auth check (cub context get), not cub info
Warns against importing Helm/ArgoCD/Flux-managed resources via this path
expectations.evidence: No mention of routing to specialized import skills for managed resources.
